what_it_measured.text: Alleviating Effects of Black Soybean Peptide on Oxidative Stress Injury Induced by Lead in PC12 Cells via Keap1/Nrf2/TXNIP Signaling Pathway

dose.text: PC12 cellscells were preincubated withwith BSP1–5 (200(200 µM)μM) for for 4 h, then treated with 10 μM lead for 24 h.
Figure 2B–D shows that 12.5–200 µM of black soybean peptide did not produce toxicity to PC12 cells (p < 0.05), so the maximum action concentration was chosen for the subsequent experiments.

endpoint.text: Protein expression of Keap1, Nrf2, and TXNIP was measured by Western blot.
Cell Viability Assay Cell viability was measured by Cell Counting Kit 8 (CCK8).
The absorbance of samples was measured five times every 5 min at 340 nm. 2.4.7.

reported_results.text: Lead can enrich the contents of MDA and ROS, but decrease the amount of CAT, SOD, GR, GPx, and GSH/GSSG in PC12 cells, while BSP can alleviate it (p < 0.05).
However, BSP treatment significantly increased the viability of PC12 cells induced by lead exposure (p < 0.05).
Compared with the Pb group, the expressions of SOD in the BSP3+Pb and BSP4+Pb groups were enhanced by 23% and 26%, and the difference was statistically significant (p < 0.05).
Black soybean peptides (BSP1, BSP3, BSP4) and VC did not significantly change the level of SOD, CAT, and MDA compared to the control group (p < 0.05) (Figure 4A–C).
Compared with the BSP1+Pb and BSP3+Pb groups, the expression level of GPx in the BSP4+Pb group was greatly enhanced, and the difference was statistically significant (p < 0.05).
However, the three black soybean peptide + Pb groups were reduced by 30%, 43%, and 88% compared with the Pb group, and the difference was statistically significant.
